title: Index-based market-wide circuit breakers introduced
description: Coordinated nationwide trading halts at 10/15/20% moves in either direction, triggered by whichever of SENSEX or NIFTY 50 breaches first. Predates the study window; included because it is the governing rule throughout it.

title: Circuit-breaker halt followed by a pre-open call auction
description: Resumption of trading after a market-wide circuit-breaker halt is preceded by a 15-minute pre-open call auction session. Predates the study window; governing rule throughout it.

title: Physical settlement of stock derivatives — phase 1
description: Bottom 50 stocks in the derivatives segment move to compulsory physical settlement from the April 2019 expiry. Framework issued 2018-12-31 under the April 2018 review of the derivatives framework.

title: Physical settlement of stock derivatives — phase 2
description: Next 50 stocks from the bottom move to compulsory physical settlement from the July 2019 expiry.

title: Physical settlement of stock derivatives — all stocks
description: All remaining stock F&O contracts move to compulsory physical settlement from the October 2019 expiry. From this point every stock derivative in India settles by delivery, which changes expiry-week behaviour in the underlying cash market.

title: Margin pledge and re-pledge system
description: Pledged securities remain in the client's demat account with a lien marked in favour of the broker, who re-pledges to the clearing corporation. Ends the practice of transferring client securities to broker accounts for margin.

title: COVID-19 market volatility measures
description: Market-wide position limits for F&O stocks cut to 50% of existing levels on eligible names, margin increases in both cash and F&O segments, revised index derivative position limits, and a 15-minute cooling-off before dynamic price bands are flexed. Announced 2020-03-20, effective at the start of trading 2020-03-23, initially for one month.

title: COVID-19 volatility measures extended
description: The March 2020 measures were extended rather than lapsing after one month, remaining in force until 2020-08-27, and were eased progressively from November 2020.

title: Uniform nationwide stamp duty regime
description: Stamp duty on securities transactions unified under the Indian Stamp Act at 0.015% on delivery buys and 0.003% on intraday buys, sell side nil. Replaces the previous state-by-state regime. Verified in Phase 1.1 and used by the cost model.

title: Peak margin regime
description: Intraday peak margin obligation compared against margin actually available with the client, phased at 25/50/75/100% of the obligation at 3, 6, 9 and 12 months from 2020-12-01. Substantially reduced intraday leverage available to retail participants.

title: T+1 rolling settlement introduced on an optional basis
description: Exchanges permitted to offer a T+1 rolling settlement cycle from 2022-01-01 at their option.

title: T+1 phased rollout begins
description: First tranche of securities moves to T+1 from trade date 2022-02-25, starting with the lowest 100 stocks by market capitalisation; the next 500 smallest were added on the last Friday of each subsequent month.

title: T+1 rollout complete
description: All listed securities trading on a T+1 settlement cycle by the end of January 2023. India became the first major equity market to complete this migration. Effective date is month-precision: the final tranche moved on the last Friday of January 2023.

title: NSE cash transaction charge cut ~1%
description: NSE cash market transaction charge reduced from 0.00325% to 0.00322% of turnover. Verified in Phase 1.1 and used by the cost model.

title: SEBI true-to-label uniform member charges
description: Exchange transaction charges made uniform irrespective of member turnover, taking the NSE cash rate to 0.00297% (Rs 2.97 per lakh per side). Verified in Phase 1.1 and used by the cost model.

title: STT raised on futures and options
description: Securities Transaction Tax on the sale of futures raised from 0.0125% to 0.02% of traded price, and on the sale of options from 0.0625% to 0.1% of premium. Announced in the July 2024 Union Budget. EQUITY DELIVERY STT WAS NOT CHANGED and remains 0.1% on both legs.

title: Equity index derivatives framework — first tranche
description: Minimum contract size for index derivatives raised from roughly Rs 5-10 lakh to Rs 15-20 lakh, the first revision in nine years; weekly expiry contracts limited to one benchmark index per exchange; upfront collection of option premium from buyers.

title: Equity index derivatives framework — intraday position limits
description: Intraday monitoring of position limits for equity index derivatives by exchanges, together with the removal of calendar spread treatment on expiry days and increased tail risk coverage on expiry. Falls inside the P1 holdout year and outside the P2 development window.
